# ezghcloud_database_user (Resource)

A user of a database with one preset on one logical database. Its password is generated and kept in a Secret in the project. Destroying it deletes the user and its Secret; tables it created stay.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `database_id` (String) Database (dbi_) it lives in. Changing it replaces the user.
- `logical_database` (String) The logical database the preset grants access to. Changing it replaces the user.
- `name` (String) Username: a lowercase letter, then up to 31 lowercase letters, digits and underscores. Changing it replaces the user.
- `preset` (String) readOnly, readWrite or owner. Changes in place.
- `project_id` (String) Project of the database. Changing it replaces the user.

### Read-Only

- `failure_code` (String) Why the user's last operation failed, as a code; null when it didn't.
- `failure_message` (String) Why the user's last operation failed; null when it didn't.
- `id` (String) database_id/name.
- `organization_id` (String) Organization managed by the configured provider.
- `secret_id` (String) The Secret (sec_) holding the user's username, password, host, port, database, engine and connection uri. Null after a drop the engine refused, until the next apply rotates the user for a new one. Terraform state never holds the password.
- `status` (String) What the user is doing: creating, available, missing (absent from the engine, for example dropped in SQL; the next apply makes it again), failed (the next apply replaces it), and others while it changes.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_database_user.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/DATABASE_ID/NAME'
```
